recipes.name: Qing Tang (Clear Chicken Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, golden and gently savoury, with the sweetness of long-simmered chicken, a little depth from pork bone and ham, and a clean finish of ginger.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light stock that carries protein, gelatin and some minerals drawn from the bones, with very little fat once it is skimmed.

ingredients.cutPrep: whole, rinsed, cut into 4 to 6 pieces
pork neck or back bones, soaked 1 hour

ingredients.prepNote: optional, for the classic Cantonese depth

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Put the chicken pieces and pork bones in a large pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Boil 1 to 2 minutes, then drain and rinse every piece and the pot.
Return the chicken, bones and ham to the clean pot with 4.5 litres of cold water, the ginger and the scallions.
Bring slowly to a bare simmer over medium heat, skimming off any foam as it rises.
Keep the pot at the gentlest simmer, about 195°F to 200°F (90°C to 93°C), partly covered, for 4 to 5 hours. Never let it boil hard, which clouds the stock.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool, and lift off the fat once it sets. It makes about 3 litres, 12 cups.
Keep it refrigerated up to 5 days or frozen up to 3 months, and season each dish rather than the stock.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken and the collagen of the pork bones, drawn into the liquid.
Low as made, since the stock is left unsalted.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Judy's Homemade Chicken Stock
The Woks of Life, Chinese Pork Stock

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life chicken stock (whole chicken, ginger, scallion, 18 cups cold water, 4 to 6 hours) blanched and simmered the Cantonese way, with pork bones from their pork stock and a piece of Jinhua ham, which is how a Cantonese kitchen builds a clear stock. 4.5 litres of water reduces to about 3 litres, so 12 servings of 1 cup. Unsalted on purpose so every dish salts itself.

recipes.name: Pork Bone Stock
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, rounded and lightly sweet, the quiet savoury base that sits under noodle soups and braises.
recipes.healthBenefit: A simple bone stock that brings gelatin and a little protein with almost no fat once skimmed.

ingredients.cutPrep: cold, plus more for soaking and blanching

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Soak the bones in cold water for 1 to 2 hours, changing the water once.
Cover the bones with fresh cold water, bring to a boil, and boil 1 minute. Drain and rinse the bones well.
Heat the oil in the clean pot over medium heat and fry the ginger and scallion for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the bones and 12 cups of cold water. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Simmer partly covered for 2 to 3 hours, skimming now and then, until it has reduced to about 8 cups.
Strain, season lightly with salt, and cool. Keep it refrigerated up to 5 days or frozen up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: Gelatin from the pork neck bones, which gives the stock its body.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Chinese Pork Stock

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life pork stock as written: 3 lb neck bones, 12 cups water, oil, scallion, ginger, salt, soaked, blanched, then simmered 2 to 3 hours. They give 8 servings; 12 cups of water reduces to about 8 cups, so 8 servings of 1 cup.

recipes.name: Lu Shui (Master Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep, glossy and sweet-savoury, with soy, rock sugar and a warm perfume of star anise, cassia and tangerine peel.
recipes.healthBenefit: A braising liquid rather than something to drink: it flavours meat, tofu and eggs, and it is high in sodium and sugar, so a little goes a long way.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.name: mei gui lu jiu (Chinese rose wine)

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.cutPrep: one 7 cm piece of cassia bark

instructions: Tie the star anise, cassia, tangerine peel, cloves and Sichuan peppercorns in a square of muslin.
Put the water, both soy sauces, rock sugar, Shaoxing wine and rose wine in a deep pot with the ginger, scallion and spice bag.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 20 to 30 minutes until the sugar has dissolved and the spices have bloomed.
Use it to poach or braise: hold meat at a bare simmer, about 205°F to 210°F (96°C to 99°C), then let it steep off the heat.
After each use, bring the stock back to a boil, skim, strain and cool it. Refrigerate up to 1 week or freeze, topping up the soy, sugar and spices as it is used.

nutritionHighlights.note: High, from the light and dark soy sauces; most stays in the pot rather than in the meat.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Soy Sauce Chicken
Wikipedia, Master stock

recipes.curationNote: The poaching liquid from Woks of Life soy sauce chicken (ginger, scallion, star anise, rose wine, Shaoxing, 2 cups light soy, 1/2 cup dark soy, 1 3/4 cups rock sugar, 12 cups water), with the cassia, tangerine peel and cloves that Wikipedia master stock lists for the Cantonese and Teochew lou mei style. About 4 litres, so 16 servings of 1 cup.

recipes.name: Hong You (Sichuan Chili Oil)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fragrant, toasty red oil with a gentle burn, a numbing hum of Sichuan pepper, and crunchy chili flakes at the bottom of the jar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly oil, so it is rich and used by the spoonful; the chili brings capsaicin and a little vitamin A.
instructions: Put the chili flakes and salt in a heatproof bowl or jar.
Put the oil, star anise, cassia, bay, Sichuan peppercorns, black cardamom, sand ginger, cloves, garlic and shallot in a small pot.
Heat over medium low until the oil reaches 200°F to 225°F (93°C to 107°C), then keep it there for 30 to 60 minutes, until the shallot and garlic are golden.
Strain out the aromatics and raise the oil to 250°F to 350°F (120°C to 175°C); the lower end gives a brighter red, the higher a toastier flavour.
Pour the hot oil over the chili flakes in two or three additions, stirring. Cool, cover, and keep in a cool cupboard up to a month or the refrigerator up to 6 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: Almost all from the rapeseed oil.
A little, from the red chili flakes.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, How to Make Chili Oil
Wikipedia, Sichuan pepper

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life chili oil: 1.5 to 3 cups oil infused at 200 to 225°F for 30 to 60 minutes with star anise, cassia, bay, Sichuan peppercorns, black cardamom, sand ginger, cloves, garlic and shallot, poured over 65 to 110 g flakes at 250 to 350°F. Taken at 2 cups oil and 90 g flakes, which fills about 2 1/2 cups, so 40 servings of 1 tbsp. Cloves kept at 1 tsp rather than 2.

recipes.name: Ginger Scallion Sauce
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright, sharp and aromatic, the green bite of scallion and the heat of fresh ginger softened by sizzling hot oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rich in oil, so a spoonful is the serving, and fresh ginger and scallion bring a little vitamin K.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the scallion, ginger and salt in a heatproof bowl and let them sit 5 to 10 minutes so the salt draws out a little juice.
Heat the oil in a small pan until it shimmers, about 350°F to 375°F (175°C to 190°C).
Pour the hot oil over the scallion and ginger; it will sizzle hard. Stir well.
Cool and serve with poached chicken, noodles or rice. Keep refrigerated up to 1 week.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the oil, which carries the flavour.
A little, from the scallion greens.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Raw Ginger Scallion Oil
The Woks of Life, Ginger Scallion Oil with Chilies

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life raw ginger scallion oil (50 g scallion, 20 g ginger, 80 to 120 ml oil, 1/2 tsp salt, 8 servings) doubled and finished the Cantonese way with hot oil poured over, which is the version served with Hainan chicken and white cut chicken; their cooked version with chilies was compared for the method. About 20 tablespoons, so 20 servings of 1 tbsp.

recipes.name: Dumpling Dipping Sauce
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, tangy and a little sweet, with black vinegar up front, raw garlic, and a slick of chili oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: A small-dose condiment: it seasons well for few calories but is high in sodium from the soy sauce.

components.note: stirred in with some of the flakes

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Dissolve the sugar in the hot water in a small bowl.
Stir in the soy sauce, black vinegar, garlic, sesame oil and chili oil.
Sprinkle in the sesame seeds and let it sit 10 to 15 minutes so the garlic mellows.
Serve in small dishes beside dumplings. Keep refrigerated up to 1 week.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the soy sauce; a tablespoon is plenty for a plate of dumplings.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Dumpling Sauce
Wikipedia, Jiaozi

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life dumpling sauce (sugar, hot water, soy, vinegar, chili oil, garlic, sesame seeds, sesame oil, 4 servings) scaled up, with Chinkiang black vinegar in place of rice vinegar because Wikipedia jiaozi names black vinegar and soy as the northern dip. Hong You makes 40 servings of 1 tbsp, so 1.5 is 1 1/2 tbsp. About 16 tablespoons in all.

recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Sauce
recipes.flavorProfile: Glossy, tangy and sweet, with tomato and pineapple fruitiness and a soft warmth of star anise and ginger.
recipes.healthBenefit: A sweet sauce, high in sugar, best used to coat rather than to pool on the plate.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Heat the oil in a small pot over medium low heat and fry the ginger and star anise for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and stir 1 minute.
Add the sugar, water, vinegar, soy sauce and pineapple juice, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved and the sauce has reduced slightly. Remove the ginger and star anise.
Stir the slurry and drizzle it in, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon, about 1 minute. Cool and refrigerate up to 2 weeks.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cane sugar and pineapple juice; this is the sweetest of the bases.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Sweet and Sour Sauce
Wikipedia, Sweet and sour

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life sweet and sour sauce as written (oil, ginger, star anise, 1/4 cup tomato paste, 2/3 cup sugar, 2/3 cup water, 3/4 cup white vinegar, soy, optional pineapple juice, cornstarch slurry, about 10 minutes). Cantonese gu lo yuk style per Wikipedia sweet and sour. They give 8 servings; it measures about 2 1/2 cups, so 10 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Black Bean Garlic Sauce
recipes.flavorProfile: Deeply savoury and funky, salty fermented black beans mellowed in garlic-scented oil with a touch of sweetness and chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: A strong-flavoured seasoning used by the spoonful; the fermented beans bring savoury depth and the sauce is high in sodium.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Rinse the black beans briefly to take off excess salt, drain, and chop them roughly.
Warm the oil in a small pot over medium low heat. Add the shallot, garlic and ginger and cook gently 3 to 5 minutes until soft and just golden.
Add the black beans and chili and cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce and sugar and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until glossy.
Cool and keep in a clean jar in the refrigerator up to 1 month, with the oil covering the top.

nutritionHighlights.note: High, from the salted fermented black beans and soy sauce.

citations.source: Wikipedia, Douchi

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from standard Cantonese proportions and the Wikipedia douchi description (salted fermented black soybeans, used with garlic for steamed spare ribs, clams and stir-fries); the Woks of Life black bean garlic sauce page had no recipe card to follow. About 1 1/4 cups, so 20 servings of 1 tbsp.

recipes.name: XO Sauce
recipes.flavorProfile: Luxurious and intensely savoury, sweet-salty dried scallop and shrimp with ham, shallot and garlic, chewy and crisp in a warm chili oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich condiment with protein from the dried seafood and ham, but high in oil and sodium, so it is used by the spoonful.
instructions: Soak the dried scallops and dried shrimp separately in the Shaoxing wine and a little water for 4 to 8 hours or overnight, then drain, keeping the liquid. Shred the scallops and chop the shrimp.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep pot to about 225°F (107°C). Fry the scallops 5 minutes, lift them out, then fry the shrimp 12 to 15 minutes until crisp at the edges, and lift them out.
Fry the ham for 2 to 3 minutes and the chilies for 2 to 3 minutes, lifting each out in turn.
Fry the shallots 8 to 10 minutes until golden, then the garlic 8 to 10 minutes until golden, keeping the oil at a gentle bubble.

Return everything to the oil with the stock, soaking liquid, brown sugar, dark soy sauce, fish sauce and chili flakes. Simmer gently 10 to 15 minutes until the liquid has cooked off and the oil runs clear.
Cool and pack into clean jars with oil covering the top. Keep refrigerated up to 2 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the dried scallops, dried shrimp and ham.
High, from the dried seafood, ham, soy and fish sauce.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, XO Sauce
Wikipedia, XO sauce

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life XO sauce halved (their full batch is 300 g each of dried scallops and shrimp, 14 shallots, 3 heads garlic, 200 g Jinhua ham, 1 3/4 cups stock, 7 cups oil, 50 servings), fried in stages at about 225°F. Hong Kong origin per Wikipedia. Qing Tang makes 12 servings of 1 cup, so 210 ml is 0.85. The half batch fills about 5 cups, so 40 servings of 2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Jiaozi Wrappers (Dumpling Dough)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, springy and slightly chewy once boiled, with a plain wheat taste that lets the filling lead.
recipes.healthBenefit: A simple flour and water dough that brings starch for energy and a little protein, with no fat added.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Put the flour in a bowl and stir in the water a little at a time with chopsticks until shaggy flakes form.
Knead 5 to 10 minutes into a smooth, firm dough. Cover and rest 30 to 60 minutes.
Knead briefly again, divide in four, and roll each into a rope about 2.5 cm thick.
Cut each rope into 12 pieces of about 12 g, press each flat, and roll into a 8 to 9 cm round, thinner at the edge than the middle.
Dust with flour and keep covered so they do not dry out. Use the same day or freeze them filled.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Dumpling Wrapper Recipe
Wikipedia, Jiaozi

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life dumpling wrapper dough: all-purpose flour and water at about 55% hydration, rested, rolled thinner at the edges. 400 g flour and 220 ml water gives about 620 g of dough, 48 wrappers of 12 to 13 g.

recipes.name: Wonton Wrappers
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, silky and tender, with a slippery bite once cooked in broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: A thin wheat wrapper that brings starch and a little protein, with no fat added.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, bread flour

instructions: Mix the flour and water into a stiff, shaggy dough, then knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Wrap it and rest 1 to 2 hours, so the gluten relaxes and it rolls thin.
Roll the dough out on a cornstarch-dusted counter, turning and dusting often, until you can almost see your hand through it, about 1 mm.
Cut into 9 cm squares and stack them with a dusting of cornstarch between each.
Wrap tightly and refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 2 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the high-protein flour that gives the wrapper its stretch.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, How to Make Wonton Wrappers
Wikipedia, Wonton

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life wonton wrappers: high-protein flour, water at about 55%, rested 2 hours, rolled paper thin with cornstarch, cut in squares. Their recipe uses an egg in some versions; kept to flour and water as written on their page. About 60 squares of 9 cm.

recipes.name: Bao Dough (Steamed Bun Dough)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy, soft and faintly sweet, with a fine white crumb that pulls apart in layers.
recipes.healthBenefit: A steamed rather than fried or baked bread, bringing starch and a little protein with almost no fat.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water and leave 5 to 10 minutes until it foams.
Mix in the flour and baking powder and knead 10 to 15 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Cover and let it rise in a warm spot 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until doubled.
Punch it down, knead 2 to 3 minutes to press out the air, and divide into 10 pieces of about 80 g.
Shape or fill each piece, set it on parchment in a steamer, and let it rise another 15 to 30 minutes.
Steam over boiling water 12 to 20 minutes depending on size. Turn off the heat and wait 3 to 5 minutes before lifting the lid, so the buns do not collapse.

nutritionHighlights.note: Almost none, since the buns are steamed.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, All-Purpose Chinese Bun Dough (Man Tou)
Wikipedia, Baozi

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life all-purpose bun dough (flour, instant yeast, a little sugar, baking powder, lukewarm water, 2 hour rise, steamed about 15 minutes). 500 g flour and 300 ml water is about 820 g of dough, so 10 buns of about 80 g.

recipes.name: Har Gow Wrapper Dough
recipes.flavorProfile: Translucent, chewy and delicately springy, and nearly tasteless, so the shrimp shows through.
recipes.healthBenefit: A starch dough made with wheat starch, bringing quick energy and very little protein.
instructions: Mix the wheat starch and cornstarch in a heatproof bowl.
Pour in the boiling water all at once and stir hard with chopsticks until it comes together. Cover and let it steam 5 minutes.
Add the lard and knead while warm, 3 to 5 minutes, into a smooth, glossy dough.
Roll into a log, cut into 24 pieces of about 15 g, and keep them covered.
Press each piece flat with the side of an oiled cleaver into a thin 7 to 8 cm round just before filling.

nutritionHighlights.note: Starch from the wheat starch and cornstarch.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Har Gow (Crystal Shrimp Dumplings)
Wikipedia, Har gow

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life har gow dough: wheat starch with a share of cornstarch (they also use tapioca), scalded with boiling water and enriched with lard. Wheat starch is washed of most of its gluten but is not certified gluten-free. About 360 g dough, 24 wrappers of 15 g.

recipes.name: Hand-Pulled Noodle Dough
recipes.flavorProfile: Bouncy, chewy and springy noodles with a clean wheat flavour and a slippery surface.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain wheat noodle that brings starch for energy and some protein, with little fat.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

instructions: Dissolve the salt in the water and stir it into the flour until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead 10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 20 to 30 minutes, then knead 2 to 3 minutes more.
Repeat the rest and knead once more, then divide into 4 to 8 pieces and roll each into a thick strip or log.
Brush every piece with oil, cover tightly, and rest at least 1 hour and up to 4, until very relaxed.
Press each piece flat, take both ends, and pull and slap it on the counter until it is long and thin, then fold and pull again for thinner noodles.
Drop them straight into boiling water and cook 1 to 3 minutes until they float and are just tender.

nutritionHighlights.note: Some, from the gluten that lets the noodles stretch.

citations.source: Omnivore's Cookbook, Hand-Pulled Noodles
Wikipedia, Lamian

recipes.curationNote: Omnivore's Cookbook hand-pulled noodle dough: 330 g all-purpose flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 240 ml water, oil, rested and kneaded in rounds, then rested long under oil before pulling. Traditional Lanzhou shops add penghui (alkaline ash) for spring; this home method uses long resting instead, as the source does. Their batch serves 4.

recipes.name: Spring Roll Wrappers
recipes.flavorProfile: Paper-thin and plain, frying up blistered, crisp and shattering.
recipes.healthBenefit: A very thin wheat wrapper that is mostly starch; once fried it carries the oil, so spring rolls are a treat.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, bread flour

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and water into a very soft, wet dough and beat it with your hand 5 to 10 minutes until it is stretchy and glossy.
Cover and rest 2 to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat a flat pan over low heat. Hold the dough in one hand and quickly rub it in a circle on the pan, then lift it away, leaving a thin film about 20 cm across.
Cook 20 to 40 seconds until the edges lift and it is dry but still white, then peel it off.
Stack the wrappers under a damp cloth as you go. Use the same day or freeze them in a sealed bag.

citations.source: Wikipedia, Spring roll

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from standard proportions: the wet, slack flour and water dough rubbed on a hot plate is the classic Shanghai chun juan pi method described on Wikipedia spring roll. No recipe page could be opened for the wrapper itself. About 24 wrappers of 20 cm.

recipes.name: Steamed Jasmine Rice
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, fluffy and fragrant grains with a light floral scent.
recipes.healthBenefit: Plain white rice is a gentle, easily digested source of starch with almost no fat.
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water 2 or 3 times, swirling, until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
Put the rice and water in a heavy pot and bring to a boil over medium high heat.
Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook 15 to 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let it stand covered 5 to 10 minutes, then fluff with a paddle.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, How to Cook Jasmine Rice

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life stovetop jasmine rice: rinsed, about 1.2 parts water to rice by weight, boiled then covered on low about 15 minutes, rested. Jasmine rice resolves to long-grain white rice. 400 g raw rice gives about 6 cups cooked.

recipes.name: Steamed Glutinous Rice
recipes.flavorProfile: Chewy, sticky and glossy grains that hold together, with a mild sweetness.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sticky rice is a dense source of starch with almost no fat, and it is gluten-free despite its name.
instructions: Rinse the glutinous rice, then cover it with cold water and soak 6 to 24 hours.
Drain it well and spread it on a cloth or parchment in a steamer basket.
Steam over boiling water 30 to 45 minutes, sprinkling a little water over the top halfway through, until the grains are tender and translucent.
Use it warm, for lo mai gai, zongzi fillings or stir-fried sticky rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: Starch from the glutinous rice, which is mostly amylopectin and so very sticky.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, How to Make Sticky Rice

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life sticky rice: soaked 6 to 24 hours, steamed 30 to 45 minutes. The soaking water is drained, so very little counts. 400 g raw gives about 4 cups.

recipes.name: Plain Congee (Jook)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, smooth and mild, a soft rice porridge that takes on whatever is stirred in.
recipes.healthBenefit: A gentle, well-hydrated rice porridge that is easy to digest, and low in fat as made.
instructions: Rinse the rice, drain it, and freeze it in a bag at least 2 hours; the frozen grains break apart and cook fast.
Bring the water and ginger to a rolling boil in a heavy pot.
Add the frozen rice straight in and return to a boil, then cook at a lively simmer 20 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until the grains have burst and it is creamy.
Season with salt, remove the ginger, and thin with hot water if it gets too thick.

nutritionHighlights.note: Starch from the rice, spread through a lot of water.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, 20-Minute Congee
Wikipedia, Congee

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life 20-minute congee method (frozen rinsed rice into boiling water, about 11 parts water to rice) for the plain base, with ginger as Cantonese jook usually carries. 150 g rice and 1.65 L water makes about 6 cups.

recipes.name: Pao Cai (Sichuan Pickled Vegetables)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, sour and lightly salty, with a gentle tingle of Sichuan pepper and warmth of chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: A brine-fermented vegetable pickle that brings live lactic acid bacteria when eaten unheated, though it is salty, so a small dish is the serving.
instructions: Boil the water with the salt and rock sugar until dissolved, then cool it completely.
Wash and fully dry the vegetables, then cut the cabbage, carrot and daikon. Wet vegetables can spoil the brine.
Pack the vegetables, ginger, fresh and dried chilies and Sichuan pepper into a very clean pickle jar.
Pour in the cooled brine and baijiu to cover everything, weigh the vegetables down, and seal. Fill the water moat if the jar has one.
Ferment at 68°F to 75°F (20°C to 24°C) for 3 to 7 days, until pleasantly sour.
Refrigerate once it tastes right. Lift pickles out with clean chopsticks and top the jar up with fresh vegetables to keep the brine going.

nutritionHighlights.note: Some, from the cabbage and radish, which is kept because they are never cooked.

citations.source: Wikipedia, Pao cai
The Woks of Life, Pickled Cabbage

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from standard brine proportions (about 5% salt, a little rock sugar and baijiu, Sichuan pepper, chilies and ginger) and the Wikipedia pao cai description of the Sichuan pickle jar. The Woks of Life pickled cabbage page is a quick vinegar pickle and was only read for context. Tier moderate since the fermentation benefit depends on how it is kept. About 3 cups of drained pickle, 12 servings of 1/4 cup.

recipes.name: Five-Spice Powder
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, sweet and aromatic, with anise and fennel up front, cassia sweetness, and a faint numbing finish.
recipes.healthBenefit: A spice blend used in small amounts that adds flavour with almost no calories or sodium.
instructions: Toast all the whole spices in a dry pan over medium low heat for 2 to 4 minutes, shaking, until fragrant.
Cool completely on a plate.
Grind to a fine powder in a spice grinder, then sift out any large pieces and grind them again.
Keep in a sealed jar away from light and use within 3 to 6 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: A trace, from the ground seeds and bark.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, How to Make Five-Spice Powder

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life five-spice: cassia, fennel, Sichuan pepper, cloves and star anise, toasted and ground. Their amounts kept. About 6 tbsp of powder, so 12 servings of 1/2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Sichuan Pepper Salt
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, toasty and floral, with the buzzing, mouth-tingling numbness of Sichuan pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: A dipping salt used by the pinch; it is almost all sodium, so a little goes a long way.

ingredients.name: Sichuan peppercorns
ingredients.cutPrep: red Sichuan peppercorns, stems and seeds picked out

instructions: Toast the salt in a dry pan over medium low heat 3 to 5 minutes until it turns faintly grey and very dry.
Add the Sichuan peppercorns and toast 1 to 2 minutes more, shaking, until fragrant but not smoking.
Cool completely, then grind together to a fine powder.
Keep in a sealed jar and use within 3 months, as a dip for fried foods and roasted meats.

nutritionHighlights.note: Almost all of this blend is salt.

citations.source: Wikipedia, Sichuan pepper

recipes.curationNote: Written from the standard jiao yan proportion (about one part peppercorn to two of salt by volume, toasted and ground together) described on Wikipedia Sichuan pepper; no recipe page could be opened. About 4 tbsp, so 8 servings of 1/2 tbsp.

recipes.name: Char Siu (Cantonese Barbecued Pork)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sticky, glossy and sweet-savoury, with caramelised edges, a honeyed lacquer, and tender, juicy pork inside.
recipes.healthBenefit: A good source of protein from pork shoulder, though it is sweet and salty from the glaze, so it is used in modest portions.

ingredients.cutPrep: pork shoulder (butt), cut in strips 5 cm thick

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 cube red fermented bean curd, mashed

instructions: Mix the sugar, salt, five-spice, white pepper, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, hoisin, molasses, garlic and fermented bean curd into a marinade.
Coat the pork strips well, cover, and refrigerate at least 8 hours and up to 24.
Heat the oven to 475°F (246°C). Set the pork on a rack over a tray lined with foil and a little water.
Roast 10 minutes, then lower to 375°F (190°C) and roast 20 to 25 minutes, turning once and basting with the leftover marinade.
Warm the maltose with the hot water and brush it over the pork. Roast 10 to 15 minutes more, until glossy and charred at the edges and the centre reads 145°F to 160°F (63°C to 71°C).
Rest 10 minutes before slicing across the grain.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the marinade and the maltose glaze.

Wikipedia, Char siu

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life char siu as written (3 lb pork shoulder, sugar, salt, five-spice, white pepper, sesame oil, Shaoxing, soy, hoisin, molasses, garlic, red fuyu, maltose glaze, 475 then 375°F, about 50 minutes). recipes.name: Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, snappy whole shrimp wrapped in a translucent, chewy skin, with a hint of bamboo shoot crunch and sesame.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp brings lean protein and selenium, and steaming keeps the fat low.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and deveined, half chopped, half in chunks

instructions: Pat the shrimp very dry. Chop half finely and cut the rest in 1 cm chunks.
Mix the shrimp with the salt, sugar, white pepper, sesame oil, oil and cornstarch, stirring one way 2 to 3 minutes until sticky. Fold in the bamboo shoots and chill 30 minutes.
Press each piece of wrapper dough into a thin round, set a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre, and pleat one side against the other to close it in a crescent.
Set the dumplings on parchment in a bamboo steamer, spaced so they do not touch.
Steam over boiling water 6 to 8 minutes, until the skins are translucent and the shrimp pink. Serve at once.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Har Gow (Crystal Shrimp Dumplings)
Wikipedia, Har gow

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life har gow filling (shrimp, half minced, half chunked, bamboo shoots, salt, sugar, white pepper, sesame oil, oil, cornstarch), steamed about 6 minutes, with the dough from the Har Gow base, 24 wrappers. Wikipedia har gow confirms the Guangzhou teahouse form. 24 dumplings, 6 servings of 4.

recipes.name: Siu Mai (Pork and Shrimp Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Juicy, savoury pork and springy shrimp in an open-topped yellow wrapper, with earthy shiitake and a bouncy bite.
recipes.healthBenefit: A good source of protein from pork and shrimp, steamed rather than fried, though pork belly makes it rich.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: very finely diced, for the tops

instructions: Mix the pork with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, salt, white pepper, sesame oil and ginger.
Stir in one direction 3 to 5 minutes, adding the water a little at a time, until the meat is sticky and pale.
Fold in the shrimp, shiitake and cornstarch and chill 20 to 30 minutes.
Hold a wrapper in a loose circle between thumb and finger, fill it with a heaped tablespoon, and squeeze it into a waisted cup, open at the top. Smooth the top and dot it with carrot.
Steam on parchment over boiling water 8 to 10 minutes, until the pork is cooked through.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the ground pork, which keeps the filling juicy.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Siu Mai
Wikipedia, Shumai

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life siu mai (ground pork, shrimp, soaked shiitake, soy, oyster sauce, Shaoxing, sugar, sesame oil, white pepper, cornstarch), steamed about 10 minutes; they use store wonton wrappers trimmed round, so the Wonton Wrappers base is the component, 30 of its 60. 30 siu mai, 6 servings of 5.

recipes.name: Char Siu Bao (Barbecued Pork Buns)
recipes.flavorProfile: A fluffy, sweet, split-topped bun around sticky, sweet-savoury barbecued pork in a glossy oyster sauce gravy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and the bun is steamed, though the filling is sweet, so these are a treat.

ingredients.cutPrep: extra, about 1 tsp, for the dough

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Make the bao dough with the extra sugar and baking powder kneaded in, and let it rise until doubled, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Fry the shallot in the oil 1 to 2 minutes, then add the stock, oyster sauce, light and dark soy, sugar and sesame oil and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry until very thick, 1 minute, then stir in the diced char siu. Cool the filling completely.
Divide the dough into 10 pieces, roll each into a 10 cm round, and pleat it closed around a heaped tablespoon of filling.
Set each bun on a square of parchment and rest 15 minutes, then steam over high heat 12 to 15 minutes, until risen and split on top.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Steamed BBQ Pork Buns (Char Siu Bao)
Wikipedia, Cha siu bao

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life char siu bao: a sweeter, more strongly leavened dough so the tops burst, and a filling of diced char siu in a shallot, oyster sauce, soy and stock gravy thickened with cornstarch. The Bao Dough base takes the extra sugar and baking powder. About 300 g char siu is 2.5 of the 8 servings of 120 g; 120 ml stock is 0.5 cup. 10 buns.

recipes.name: Jiaozi (Pork and Napa Cabbage Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender boiled dumplings with a juicy, gingery pork and sweet napa cabbage filling, dipped in tangy black vinegar sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and napa cabbage adds vitamin C and K, and boiling keeps added fat low.

ingredients.cutPrep: finely chopped, salted and squeezed dry

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Toss the chopped napa with half the salt, leave 15 to 20 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as you can.
Mix the pork with the ginger, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, white pepper and the rest of the salt. Stir in one direction, adding the cold stock a little at a time, until it is all absorbed and sticky.
Fold in the cabbage, scallion, sesame oil and oil.
Fill each wrapper with a heaped teaspoon, fold it in half, and pinch and pleat the edges shut.
Boil in batches in a large pot of water. When it returns to a boil, add 1 cup of cold water; repeat twice more, then lift them out once they float, 6 to 8 minutes in all.
Serve hot with the dipping sauce.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, The Dumpling Recipe You'll Ever Need
Wikipedia, Jiaozi

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life pork and napa dumplings (ground pork, salted napa, ginger, scallion, Shaoxing, soy, sesame oil, oil, white pepper, stock beaten in), boiled with the northern three additions of cold water described on Wikipedia jiaozi. Uses all 48 Jiaozi Wrappers. 48 dumplings, 8 servings of 6 with 1 tbsp of sauce each.

recipes.name: Xiao Long Bao (Soup Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Delicate, thin pleated skins that burst with hot, rich pork broth around a tender, gingery meatball, eaten with black vinegar and ginger.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and the gelatin-rich aspic bring protein, though the filling is fatty, so these are rich.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
ingredients.cutPrep: half in lengths, half finely chopped

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Simmer the pork skin with the water, the ginger slices, the scallion lengths and half the Shaoxing wine for 2 to 3 hours, until reduced by about half.
Strain it, pour it into a dish, and chill 3 to 4 hours or overnight until set firm. Dice the aspic finely.

Mix the ground pork with the minced ginger, chopped scallion, soy sauce, sugar, salt, sesame oil, white pepper and the rest of the Shaoxing, stirring one way until sticky. Fold in about 300 g of the aspic.
Set a heaped teaspoon of filling on each thin wrapper and pleat it closed with 16 to 18 folds, twisting the top shut.
Steam on parchment or napa leaves over boiling water 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve at once with the black vinegar and thin strips of fresh ginger. Bite a small hole and sip the soup first.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork and the collagen in the pork-skin aspic.
From the fatty pork and the aspic.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Steamed Shanghai Soup Dumplings (Xiaolongbao)
Wikipedia, Xiaolongbao

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life xiaolongbao: pork-skin aspic simmered and set, folded into a seasoned fatty pork filling, wrapped in very thin flour and water skins with many pleats and steamed about 8 minutes. Their skin dough is the same flour and water as the Jiaozi Wrappers base, rolled thinner, so 40 of its 48. 40 dumplings, 5 servings of 8.

recipes.name: Hong You Chao Shou (Wontons in Chili Oil)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky pork wontons slicked with fragrant chili oil, sweet soy, black vinegar and garlic, with a numbing buzz of Sichuan pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein, though the chili oil sauce adds a good deal of fat and the soy adds sodium.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Crush the ginger into the water and leave 10 minutes, then strain.
Mix the pork with the salt, Shaoxing wine and white pepper, then beat in the ginger water a little at a time until absorbed and sticky. Stir in the sesame oil.
Put a scant teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, fold it into a triangle, and bring the two far corners together, pinching them shut.
Warm the soy sauce with the sugar until dissolved, 2 to 3 minutes, to make a sweet soy, and divide it among 4 bowls with the vinegar, garlic, chili oil and ground Sichuan pepper.
Boil the wontons 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and the filling is cooked, then drain and add 10 to each bowl. Toss and top with scallion.

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life and Omnivore's Cookbook compared: pork beaten with ginger water, folded in the chao shou shape, sauced with chili oil, a quickly cooked sweet soy, black vinegar, garlic and Sichuan pepper. 40 of the 60 Wonton Wrappers; 8 tbsp of Hong You. 4 bowls of 10.

recipes.name: Guotie (Potstickers)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, golden-bottomed dumplings with tender steamed tops and a juicy pork and cabbage filling.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and cabbage adds vitamin C, though frying the bottoms adds some fat.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mix the pork with the ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, salt and white pepper and stir one way until sticky.
Fold in the cabbage, scallion and sesame oil.
Fill each wrapper with a heaped teaspoon, fold it in half, and pleat one side to seal.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and set 12 dumplings in flat side down. Fry 2 minutes until golden underneath.
Pour in 80 ml of water, cover at once, and steam 6 to 8 minutes, until the water has gone and the bottoms crisp again.
Repeat with the rest and serve crisp side up with the dipping sauce.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Easiest Pork and Cabbage Potstickers
Wikipedia, Guotie

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life pork and cabbage potstickers: fried, then steamed with water under a lid until crisp again, the method Wikipedia guotie describes. 36 of the 48 Jiaozi Wrappers. 6 servings of 6, with a tablespoon of dipping sauce each.

recipes.name: Shengjian Bao (Pan-Fried Pork Buns)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, fluffy buns with crunchy golden bottoms, sesame and scallion on top, and a juicy, soupy pork filling.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein, though the fatty filling and fried bottoms make these rich.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
ingredients.cutPrep: half for the filling, half to finish

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mix the pork with the ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, salt and white pepper. Beat in the cold stock a little at a time until absorbed, then stir in the sesame oil and half the scallion. Chill 30 minutes.
Divide the risen dough into 20 pieces of about 28 g, roll each into a round, and pleat it closed around a tablespoon of filling.
Rest the buns 10 to 15 minutes. Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium heat and set them in, pleats up or down as you like.
Fry 2 to 3 minutes until the bottoms are golden, then pour in the water, cover, and cook 7 to 8 minutes until the water has gone.
Uncover, cook 1 to 2 minutes more to crisp the bottoms, and scatter with sesame seeds and scallion.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Shanghai Pan-Fried Pork Buns (Sheng Jian Bao)

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life sheng jian bao: yeasted bun dough, a juicy pork filling with stock beaten in, fried then steamed in a covered pan and finished with sesame and scallion. Bao Dough base used at 7 of its 10 servings (560 g), cut in 20 small buns. 5 servings of 4.

recipes.name: Cheung Fun (Rice Noodle Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, slippery steamed rice sheets rolled around sweet shrimp, bathed in a light sweet soy sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp brings lean protein and the rice sheets are steamed and gluten-light, though the sauce adds sodium.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.cutPrep: light soy sauce, for the sauce

instructions: Whisk the rice flour, wheat starch, cornstarch, salt, water and oil into a thin batter and rest 30 minutes.
Simmer the soy sauce, sugar and water 2 to 3 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then stir in the sesame oil. This is the sweet soy sauce.
Bring a wok of water to a boil under a steaming rack. Oil a flat tray, stir the batter, and pour in a thin layer.
Scatter a few shrimp and some scallion over it, cover, and steam 2 to 3 minutes until the sheet is set and bubbly.
Roll it up with an oiled scraper, cut it in lengths, and repeat. Serve with the sweet soy sauce poured over.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Shrimp Rice Noodle Rolls (Cheung Fun)
Wikipedia, Rice noodle roll

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life shrimp cheung fun: rice flour with a little wheat starch and cornstarch, thin batter steamed on a tray, rolled around shrimp, with a light sweet soy sauce. 4 plates.

recipes.name: Lo Mai Gai (Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaf)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fragrant, earthy sticky rice soaked with soy and the scent of lotus leaf, hiding savoury chicken, sweet sausage and shiitake.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the rice is filling, though the sausage and oyster sauce make it rich and salty.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the chicken in half the oyster sauce and soy sauce with the Shaoxing wine, cornstarch and white pepper for 20 to 30 minutes.
Stir the rest of the oyster sauce, both soy sauces, sugar and sesame oil through the warm steamed sticky rice.
Fry the sausage, shiitake and dried shrimp in the oil 2 to 3 minutes, then add the chicken and cook 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in the scallion.
Lay a half lotus leaf out, put a portion of rice in the middle, the filling on top and more rice over it, then fold it into a tight parcel.
Steam the parcels, seam side down, 30 to 40 minutes. Open at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken thigh, sausage and dried shrimp.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Lo Mai Gai (Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaf)
Wikipedia, Lo mai gai

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life lo mai gai: soaked and steamed glutinous rice seasoned with oyster sauce, light and dark soy and sesame oil, filled with marinated chicken, lap cheong, shiitake and dried shrimp, wrapped in lotus leaves and steamed again. 600 g raw rice is 6 cups of the Steamed Glutinous Rice base. 8 parcels.

recipes.name: Lo Bak Go (Turnip Cake)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, savoury radish cake with a golden pan-fried crust, flecked with sweet sausage, dried shrimp and shiitake.
recipes.healthBenefit: Daikon brings vitamin C and the cake is mostly rice starch, though the sausage and frying make it a rich snack.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Fry the sausage, dried shrimp and shiitake in 2 tablespoons of oil for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant, then set aside.
Simmer the grated daikon with its juices and 120 ml of the water for 10 to 15 minutes, until soft and translucent.

Whisk the rice flour and cornstarch with the remaining water, salt, sugar, white pepper and sesame oil, then stir it into the hot radish off the heat with the fried mixture until it forms a thick paste.
Press it into an oiled 20 cm square pan and smooth the top.
Steam over boiling water 50 to 60 minutes, until a chopstick comes out almost clean. Cool completely, then chill several hours.
Cut it in 12 slices and pan-fry in a little oil 3 to 4 minutes a side until golden. Serve with scallion.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Turnip Cake (Lo Bak Go)
Wikipedia, Turnip cake

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life lo bak go: grated daikon cooked down, bound with rice flour, studded with lap cheong, dried shrimp and shiitake, steamed about an hour, chilled, sliced and pan-fried. Their recipe also uses Chinese bacon, left out here to keep one cured meat. 12 slices.

recipes.name: Chun Juan (Spring Rolls)
recipes.flavorProfile: Shatteringly crisp, blistered rolls around a soft, savoury filling of pork, napa cabbage and shiitake.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and cabbage bring some protein and vitamins, but deep-frying makes these a treat.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: half for the pork, half in a slurry

instructions: Toss the pork with the Shaoxing wine, half the soy sauce and half the cornstarch.
Stir-fry the pork in the oil over high heat 1 to 2 minutes, then add the shiitake, carrot and napa and cook 3 to 4 minutes until wilted.
Season with the oyster sauce, the rest of the soy sauce, salt, white pepper and sesame oil, then thicken with the rest of the cornstarch in a little water. Cool completely.
Roll a heaped tablespoon of filling in each wrapper, tucking in the sides, and seal the edge with a dab of flour paste.
Deep-fry at 350°F to 360°F (175°C to 180°C) 3 to 5 minutes until golden and blistered. Drain and serve hot.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Shanghai-Style Spring Rolls
Wikipedia, Spring roll

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life Shanghai spring rolls: julienned pork, napa and shiitake in a thickened sauce, rolled in thin wrappers and deep-fried. Oil absorbed estimated at about 60 ml. 20 rolls, 10 servings of 2.

recipes.name: Cong You Bing (Scallion Pancakes)
recipes.flavorProfile: Flaky, chewy layered flatbreads with crisp golden edges and pockets of fragrant scallion.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly wheat starch and oil, so these are filling and rich rather than light.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Stir the boiling water into the flour, then the cold water, and knead 5 to 8 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil until hot and pour it over 2 tablespoons of flour and the salt, stirring into a smooth paste.
Divide the dough in 4. Roll each piece thin, spread it with the paste, scatter with scallion, then roll it up like a rope and coil it into a snail.
Rest the coils 10 to 15 minutes, then roll each out gently to a 20 cm round.
Fry in the remaining oil over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Push the sides in to loosen the layers and cut in wedges.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the oil paste and frying oil.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Shanghai Scallion Pancakes
Wikipedia, Scallion pancake

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life Shanghai scallion pancakes: hot and cold water dough, an oil and flour paste spread before rolling and coiling, shallow-fried. 4 pancakes of about 20 cm.

recipes.name: Jiu Cai Jiaozi (Pork and Chive Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Juicy pork dumplings with the bright, garlicky green flavour of Chinese chives.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and Chinese chives add vitamin K and A, and boiling keeps added fat low.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mix the pork with the ginger, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, salt, sugar and white pepper, then beat in the cold stock until absorbed.
Toss the chives with the oil and sesame oil first, which keeps them from weeping, then fold them into the pork.
Fill each wrapper with a heaped teaspoon, fold, and pleat shut.
Boil in batches, adding cold water each time it returns to a boil, 6 to 8 minutes until they float, or pan-fry like potstickers.
Serve hot with the dipping sauce.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Pork and Chive Dumplings
Wikipedia, Jiaozi

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life pork and chive dumplings: chives coated in oil before mixing, pork beaten with stock. All 48 Jiaozi Wrappers. 8 servings of 6 with 1 tbsp of sauce each.

recipes.name: Su Baozi (Vegetable Buns)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy steamed buns around a savoury, gingery filling of bok choy, shiitake, tofu and glass noodles.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plant-based bun bringing greens, mushrooms and tofu protein, steamed with little oil.

ingredients.baseName: Glass noodles made from mung bean starch
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Blanch the bok choy 30 to 60 seconds, cool it in cold water, squeeze it very dry and chop it finely.
Fry the ginger and shiitake in the oil 2 to 3 minutes, then cool.
Mix the bok choy, shiitake, tofu and glass noodles with the soy sauce, salt, sugar, white pepper and sesame oil.
Divide the risen dough into 14 pieces, roll each into a round, and pleat it closed around a heaped tablespoon of filling.
Rest 15 minutes, then steam 12 to 15 minutes. Wait 3 to 5 minutes before lifting the lid.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Steamed Vegetable Buns
Wikipedia, Baozi

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life steamed vegetable buns: bok choy, shiitake, pressed tofu and glass noodles in the all-purpose bun dough. The whole Bao Dough base cut in 14 smaller buns. Vegan as written; the soy sauce carries wheat.

recipes.name: Fun Guo (Chiuchow Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Chewy, translucent dumplings around a savoury, crunchy filling of pork, peanuts, dried shrimp and jicama.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and peanuts bring protein and the dumplings are steamed, though the dried shrimp and sauces add sodium.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Fry the dried shrimp and shiitake in the oil 1 to 2 minutes, add the pork and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes until cooked.
Add the jicama, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and white pepper and cook 1 to 2 minutes. Cool, then stir in the peanuts, cilantro and sesame oil.
Press each piece of dough into a thin round, fill it with a heaped teaspoon, and fold it into a half moon, pinching the edge shut.
Steam on parchment over boiling water 6 to 8 minutes until the skins are translucent. Serve with chili oil if you like.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork, peanuts and dried shrimp.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Steamed Crystal Dumplings (Fun Guo)
Wikipedia, Fun guo

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life Chiuchow fun guo: a cooked filling of pork, dried shrimp, shiitake, jicama, peanuts and cilantro in a wheat starch dough. Uses the whole Har Gow Wrapper Dough base. 24 dumplings, 6 servings of 4.

recipes.name: Dan Dan Mian (Dan Dan Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Spicy, numbing and nutty noodles in a pool of chili oil and sesame sauce, topped with crisp, savoury pork and preserved mustard greens.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and bok choy adds greens, though the chili oil makes this a rich bowl.

ingredients.name: sui mi ya cai (preserved mustard greens)

ingredients.baseName: Seasoning sauce, Tian Mian Jiang (sweet soybean paste)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Fry the pork in the oil over medium high heat 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and crisp. Add the Shaoxing wine, sweet bean sauce and dark soy sauce and cook 1 minute.
Add the ya cai and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes more, then set aside.
Divide the chili oil, ground Sichuan pepper, soy sauce, sesame paste, sugar and garlic among 4 bowls, with 1/4 cup of hot stock in each.
Boil the noodles until just tender, 3 to 5 minutes, and blanch the bok choy in the same water for the last 30 seconds.
Lift the noodles and greens into the bowls, top with the pork, peanuts and scallion, and toss at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork and sesame paste.
From the chili oil and pork.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Dan Dan Noodles
Wikipedia, Dandan noodles

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life dan dan: crisp pork with sui mi ya cai and sweet bean sauce, a bowl sauce of chili oil, Sichuan pepper, soy, sesame paste, sugar and stock, wheat noodles and greens. Chengdu street version per Wikipedia. 8 tbsp of Hong You, 1 cup of Qing Tang. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Zha Jiang Mian (Fried Sauce Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick wheat noodles under a dark, salty-sweet fried bean sauce with nuggets of pork belly, cooled by crunchy cucumber and sprouts.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and the raw vegetables add crunch and vitamin C, though the bean sauce is salty and the pork belly rich.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Seasoning sauce, Tian Mian Jiang (sweet soybean paste)

instructions: Fry the pork belly in the oil over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes until the fat runs and the edges brown.
Add the ginger and scallion whites and cook 1 minute, then the Shaoxing wine.
Add the sweet bean sauce, ground bean sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar and fry 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the water and simmer over low heat 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and glossy with oil on top.
Boil the noodles 3 to 5 minutes, drain, and rinse briefly if you like them springy.
Serve the noodles topped with the sauce and the cucumber, carrot, sprouts and scallion greens, mixed at the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork belly and fermented soybean sauces.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Beijing Fried Sauce Noodles (Zha Jiang Mian)
Wikipedia, Zhajiangmian

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life Beijing zha jiang mian: diced pork belly fried slowly in sweet bean sauce and ground bean sauce until oily and thick, over thick wheat noodles with raw julienned vegetables. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Gon Chow Ngau Ho (Beef Chow Fun)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, slippery wide rice noodles seared with tender beef, sprouts and scallion in a savoury soy glaze.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein and iron and the rice noodles are wheat-free, though the dish is stir-fried in plenty of oil.

ingredients.baseName: Rice, non-glutinous rice products, fresh noodles, rice noodles
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the beef with the baking soda, cornstarch, water, 1 teaspoon of soy sauce and a little oil. Marinate 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Heat a wok until smoking. Sear the beef in 1 tablespoon of oil 1 to 2 minutes until browned but pink, and lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil, then the ginger and onion, and stir-fry 1 minute.
Add the noodles, spread them out, and leave them 30 to 60 seconds to char before tossing. Add the Shaoxing wine, the remaining soy sauce, dark soy, sugar and white pepper and toss 1 to 2 minutes.
Return the beef with the sprouts and scallion and toss over high heat 1 minute. Finish with the sesame oil.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Beef Chow Fun
Wikipedia, Beef chow fun

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life beef chow fun: flank velveted with baking soda and cornstarch, seared, then fresh wide rice noodles charred with onion, ginger, sprouts and scallion in light and dark soy. Wok hei is the point of the dish, per Wikipedia. 3 plates.

recipes.name: Lo Mein
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, saucy egg noodles tossed with sweet barbecued pork, crisp greens, mushrooms and sprouts in a glossy soy and oyster sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Char siu brings protein and the vegetables add vitamins and fibre, though the sauce is salty.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Boil the noodles until just tender, 2 to 4 minutes, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the ginger, shiitake and carrot 1 minute, then the bok choy and napa 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and char siu and pour the Shaoxing wine around the edge of the wok.
Add the stock, light and dark soy, oyster sauce, sugar and white pepper and toss 2 minutes, until the noodles are evenly coloured.
Add the sprouts and scallion, toss 30 seconds, and finish with the sesame oil.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the char siu and egg noodles.
From the bok choy and carrot.

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life pork lo mein made with char siu, as Cantonese cooks do (Wikipedia lo mein): boiled egg noodles tossed with greens in soy, dark soy and oyster sauce. 240 g char siu is 2 of 8 servings. 4 plates.

recipes.name: Cantonese Crispy Chow Mein
recipes.flavorProfile: A golden, crunchy nest of pan-fried noodles softening under a savoury, glossy sauce of chicken and crisp vegetables.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken breast brings lean protein and the vegetables add vitamins, though the pan-fried noodles take up a good deal of oil.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 tsp for the chicken, the rest for the sauce

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the chicken with 1 teaspoon each of soy sauce, cornstarch and oil for 15 minutes.
Boil the noodles 1 to 2 minutes, rinse, and drain very well. Toss with the dark soy sauce.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a wide pan over medium heat, press the noodles in a flat cake, and fry 5 to 7 minutes a side until golden and crisp. Slide onto a platter.
Stir-fry the chicken in 1 tablespoon of oil 2 to 3 minutes until cooked, then lift out. Add the rest of the oil, ginger, garlic, shiitake, carrot, napa and snow peas and stir-fry 2 minutes.

Add the stock, oyster sauce, the rest of the soy, the Shaoxing wine, sugar and white pepper and bring to a boil. Return the chicken, thicken with the rest of the cornstarch in a little water, and add the sprouts, scallion and sesame oil.
Pour it over the crisp noodles and serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the snow peas and napa cabbage.

Wikipedia, Chow mein

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life gai see chow mein: thin egg noodles pan-fried into a crisp cake, topped with chicken and vegetables in a thickened stock, oyster and soy sauce. Hong Kong style per Wikipedia chow mein. 3 plates.

recipes.name: Biang Biang Mian
recipes.flavorProfile: Wide, chewy belt noodles slicked with sizzling chili oil, garlic and black vinegar, with spiced cumin lamb.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lamb brings protein, iron and zinc and bok choy adds greens, though the sizzled oil makes it rich.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the lamb with the Shaoxing wine, 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, cornstarch and half the cumin for 20 minutes.
Sear the lamb in 2 tablespoons of oil over high heat 1 to 2 minutes, add the onion and the rest of the cumin and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes more. Set aside.
Pull the rested dough into long belts 2 to 3 cm wide and boil 1 to 2 minutes until they float, blanching the bok choy in the same pot.
Divide the noodles and greens among bowls with the rest of the soy sauce, black vinegar and salt. Pile the garlic, chili flakes, Sichuan pepper and scallion on top.
Heat the remaining oil until just smoking, about 375°F (190°C), and pour it over the aromatics so they sizzle. Top with the lamb and toss.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the hot oil poured over.

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life cumin lamb biang biang: wide hand-pulled belts with hot oil poured over garlic, chili and scallion, soy and black vinegar, and cumin lamb as in Xi'an Muslim quarter shops. Hand-Pulled Noodle Dough base, all 4 servings. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Liang Pi (Cold Skin Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, slippery, chewy sheets of starch noodle with spongy gluten, crisp cucumber and a sour, spicy, garlicky dressing.
recipes.healthBenefit: A cold noodle bowl that is light in fat apart from the chili oil, with protein from the wheat gluten.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Knead the flour, salt and 270 ml water into a firm dough and rest 1 hour. Cover it with water and squeeze and knead it until the water turns milky; pour it off into a bowl and repeat until only a stretchy lump of gluten is left.
Let the starch water settle in the refrigerator 4 hours or overnight, then pour off the clear water on top.
Mix the gluten with the yeast, rest it 1 hour, and steam it 20 to 25 minutes. Cool and cut it into cubes.

Stir the starch, pour a thin layer into an oiled metal tray, and steam it over boiling water 2 to 3 minutes until set and bubbly. Cool the tray in cold water, peel the sheet out, brush it with oil and repeat.
Cut the sheets into wide strips. Toss with the gluten, cucumber, sprouts, garlic water, black vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, Sichuan pepper, chili oil and sesame oil, and top with cilantro.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Cold Skin Noodles (Liang Pi)

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life liang pi: flour dough washed to separate starch from gluten, the starch steamed in thin sheets, the gluten steamed into spongy cubes, dressed with garlic water, black vinegar, soy and chili oil. Xi'an origin per Wikipedia. 6 tbsp Hong You. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Lanzhou Niu Rou Mian (Lanzhou Beef Noodle Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, fragrant spiced beef broth with springy hand-pulled noodles, tender beef, white radish, red chili oil and green herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein and iron and the broth is light, while daikon adds a little vitamin C.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Soak the beef in cold water 1 hour, then cover with fresh water, bring to a boil and boil 2 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Put the beef in a pot with 4 litres of water, the ginger and the spices tied in muslin, and bring to a bare simmer. Skim well.
Simmer gently, uncovered, 2 to 3 hours, until the beef is tender. Lift it out, cool and slice it thin; strain the broth.
Season the broth with salt and white pepper and simmer the daikon in it 10 to 15 minutes until translucent.
Pull the noodles and boil them 1 to 3 minutes. Ladle the clear broth and radish over them in bowls, and top with beef, cilantro, scallion and a spoonful of chili oil.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Lanzhou Beef Noodle Soup
Wikipedia, Lanzhou beef noodles

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life Lanzhou beef noodle soup: shank soaked and blanched, simmered with Sichuan pepper, star anise, cassia, fennel, bay and black cardamom, clear broth, daikon, chili oil, cilantro and scallion. Wikipedia lists the one clear, two white, three red, four green, five yellow standard. Hand-Pulled Noodle Dough base scaled to 6 servings. 6 bowls.

recipes.name: Cong You Ban Mian (Scallion Oil Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Simple, deeply savoury noodles tossed in sweet soy and fragrant oil from scallions fried until dark and crisp.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain noodle dish that is mostly wheat starch and scallion-flavoured oil, so it is filling and rich rather than light.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 7 cm lengths, whites and greens apart

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Put the oil and scallion whites in a pan over medium low heat and fry 5 minutes, then add the greens.
Keep frying gently 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until the scallions are dark brown and crisp. Lift them out.
Pour in the light and dark soy and the sugar; it will bubble hard. Simmer 1 minute until the sugar dissolves, then turn off the heat.
Boil the noodles 1 to 3 minutes and drain well.
Toss the noodles with 3 to 4 tablespoons of the scallion oil sauce per bowl and top with the crisp scallions.

citations.source: Omnivore's Cookbook, Scallion Oil Noodles
Wikipedia, Scallion pancake

recipes.curationNote: Omnivore's Cookbook Shanghai scallion oil noodles: scallions slowly fried in oil until dark, then soy, dark soy and sugar added to the oil, tossed with thin fresh noodles. The Wikipedia link is for the scallion and oil technique in Shanghai cooking. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Ma Jiang Liang Mian (Cold Sesame Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, chewy noodles coated in a creamy, nutty sesame sauce with a tang of black vinegar, a little heat and crisp cucumber.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sesame paste brings calcium, healthy fats and some protein, and the cucumber adds freshness, though the sauce is rich.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Boil the noodles until just tender, 3 to 5 minutes, then rinse under cold water until cool and drain well. Toss with the sesame oil.
Whisk the sesame paste with the warm water a spoonful at a time until smooth, then whisk in the soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, garlic, ginger and chili oil.
Toss the noodles with the sauce.
Top with the cucumber, peanuts, sesame seeds and scallion and serve cold.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sesame paste and seeds.
From the sesame paste and peanuts, mostly unsaturated.

Wikipedia, Cold noodles

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life cold sesame noodles: noodles rinsed cold and oiled, Chinese sesame paste loosened with water and seasoned with soy, black vinegar, sugar, garlic and chili oil, topped with cucumber and peanuts. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Guo Qiao Mi Xian (Crossing the Bridge Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: A scalding, golden chicken and pork broth that cooks paper-thin meats, quail egg and greens at the table, poured over soft rice noodles.
recipes.healthBenefit: A varied bowl bringing protein from chicken, pork, shrimp and egg with greens and mushrooms, and a light broth.

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear fungus, dried

ingredients.name: chicken fat (from the cavity of the chicken)

instructions: Soak the rice noodles, then boil them 4 to 6 minutes until soft and divide among 4 large bowls.
Lay out the thin-sliced chicken, pork, shrimp and ham, the quail eggs, mushrooms, greens, sprouts, chives and pickle on small plates.
Bring the stock to a hard boil, season with salt and white pepper, and stir in the chicken fat so a layer of fat sits on top.
Warm large, heavy soup bowls with boiling water, empty them, and ladle in the boiling broth.
At the table, slide in the meats first, then crack in a quail egg, then add the vegetables and finally the noodles. Wait 2 to 3 minutes for everything to cook before eating.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken, pork, shrimp, ham and quail egg.
From the pea shoots and chives.

recipes.name: Re Gan Mian (Hot Dry Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Springy, chewy alkaline noodles tossed in a thick, nutty sesame sauce with soy, crunchy pickled beans and a little chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Sesame paste brings calcium and fats, though this is a rich, salty breakfast noodle.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Boil the noodles 1 to 2 minutes, until barely cooked, then drain and toss with 1 tablespoon of sesame oil. Spread them out with a fan to cool and dry.
Loosen the sesame paste with the rest of the sesame oil and the warm water until it pours thickly.
To serve, dip the noodles in boiling water 20 to 40 seconds to heat them, then shake dry.
Toss each bowl with the soy sauce, dark soy, salt, sesame sauce and chili oil, and top with the pickled beans, zha cai, scallion and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the soy sauce and pickles.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Hot Dry Noodles (Re Gan Mian)
Wikipedia, Hot dry noodles

recipes.name: Ma Yi Shang Shu (Ants Climbing a Tree)
recipes.flavorProfile: Slippery glass noodles soaked with a spicy, savoury chili bean sauce and clinging bits of minced pork.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and the mung bean noodles are wheat-free, though the chili bean paste is salty.

ingredients.baseName: Glass noodles made from mung bean starch
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Fry the pork in the oil over medium high heat 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and browned.
Add the doubanjiang and fry 1 minute until the oil turns red, then add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the Shaoxing wine, stock, light and dark soy and sugar and bring to a boil.
Add the drained noodles and simmer 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until they have soaked up most of the sauce.
Finish with the sesame oil and scallion and serve.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the doubanjiang and soy sauce.

recipes.name: Yangzhou Chao Fan (Yangzhou Fried Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy, separate grains of rice fried with egg, shrimp, ham, barbecued pork and peas, lightly seasoned so each piece comes through.
recipes.healthBenefit: Egg, shrimp and pork bring protein and the peas add fibre, making this a fuller meal than plain fried rice.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium heat, scramble the eggs until just set, and lift them out.
Add another tablespoon of oil over high heat and stir-fry the shrimp 1 minute until pink. Lift them out.
Add the last of the oil and the onion and cook 1 to 2 minutes, then the ham, char siu and peas for 1 minute.
Add the cold rice, breaking up the clumps, and stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes until hot and the grains are separate.
Season with salt, sugar, white pepper and the Shaoxing wine around the edge of the wok. Return the egg and shrimp and add the scallion and lettuce, tossing 30 seconds until the lettuce just wilts.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the egg, shrimp, ham and char siu.

recipes.name: Dan Chao Fan (Egg Fried Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden, fluffy rice with soft ribbons of egg, sweet onion, peas and scallion, seasoned simply with salt and pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs bring protein and choline, and the peas and pepper add fibre and vitamin C.

ingredients.cutPrep: beaten into the eggs for colour

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Beat the eggs with the turmeric. Scramble them in 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat until just set, break them into pieces, and lift them out.
Heat the rest of the oil over medium high heat and cook the onion 2 minutes, then the red pepper and peas 1 minute.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes, pressing out the clumps, until it is hot through.
Season with the salt, sugar and black pepper, return the egg, add the scallion and toss 1 minute more.

Wikipedia, Egg fried rice

recipes.name: Bao Zai Fan (Claypot Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rice cooked in a clay pot under sweet Chinese sausage, cured pork and marinated chicken, with a crackling, toasty crust at the bottom and a sweet soy drizzle.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the greens add vitamins, though the cured sausage and pork are salty and rich.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the chicken with the ginger, cornstarch, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce and sesame oil and leave 20 minutes.
Simmer the light soy, dark soy, rock sugar, shallot, garlic and 3 tablespoons of water 2 to 3 minutes for the sauce.
Oil the inside of the clay pot, add the drained rice and water and bring to a boil over medium heat. Cook uncovered 5 to 8 minutes until the water is level with the rice and little holes appear.
Lay the chicken, mushrooms, sausage and cured pork on top, cover, and cook over low heat 10 to 15 minutes.
Drizzle peanut oil around the edge of the pot and tilt the pot over the flame 5 to 8 minutes, turning it, until the bottom crackles and crisps.
Add the gai lan and scallion, pour the sauce over, and mix at the table, scraping up the crust.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken thigh and cured meats.
From the cured sausage, cured pork and soy sauce.

Lap cheong and lap yuk are cured with Chinese rose wine. 3 bowls.

recipes.name: Hainan Chicken Rice
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky poached chicken with rice cooked in chicken fat and broth, served with a sharp chili sauce, a pungent ginger sauce and sweet dark soy.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the broth is mild, though the rice cooked in chicken fat makes it a richer plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: sliced, plus grated for the sauces

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.name: chicken fat (from the cavity of the chicken)

instructions: Rub the chicken with salt, rinse, and lower it into a pot of boiling water with the sliced ginger and scallion. Return to a bare simmer, cover, and poach 30 to 35 minutes, until the thigh reads 165°F (74°C).
Lift the chicken into an ice bath for 10 minutes so the skin tightens, then rub it with sesame oil. Keep the broth.

Fry the shallot and half the garlic in the chicken fat 2 minutes, add the rice and fry 2 to 3 minutes, then cook it in about 720 ml of the broth with a teaspoon of salt, 15 to 20 minutes, and rest 10 minutes.
For the chili sauce, blend the chilies with some grated ginger, the rest of the garlic, the lime juice, rice vinegar, a little salt and 2 to 3 tablespoons of broth.
For the sweet soy, simmer the dark soy with the rock sugar and 3 tablespoons of water 2 to 3 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Carve the chicken and serve it on the rice with cucumber, cilantro, the three sauces and a bowl of the broth.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fresh chilies and lime.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Hainanese Chicken Rice
Wikipedia, Hainanese chicken rice

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life Hainanese chicken rice: chicken poached then chilled in ice water, rice fried in rendered chicken fat with garlic and cooked in the poaching stock, served with chili sauce, ginger sauce and sweet dark soy. The Ginger Scallion Sauce base stands in for the ginger sauce. 6 plates.

recipes.name: Pei Dan Shou Rou Zhou (Century Egg and Pork Congee)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, savoury rice porridge with tender slivers of lean pork, rich, creamy century egg, ginger and scallion.
recipes.healthBenefit: A gentle, easy to digest bowl, with protein from the pork and egg.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Marinate the pork with the salt, cornstarch, Shaoxing wine and white pepper for 15 minutes.
Bring the congee and stock to a simmer, stirring, and add half the century egg so it melts into the porridge.
Stir in the ginger and pork and simmer 3 to 5 minutes until the pork is just cooked.
Serve with the rest of the century egg, scallion, a little sesame oil and more white pepper.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork and century egg.

citations.source: Omnivore's Cookbook, Century Egg Congee
The Woks of Life, 20-Minute Congee
Wikipedia, Century egg

recipes.curationNote: Omnivore's Cookbook century egg congee and Woks of Life 20-minute congee compared. Omnivore's Cookbook uses chicken thigh; the dish name calls for lean pork (shou rou), so pork tenderloin is used. Plain Congee base, 4 cups, with 2 cups Qing Tang. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Yu Pian Zhou (Fish Congee)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, creamy rice porridge with soft, silky slices of white fish, sharp ginger and fresh greens.
recipes.healthBenefit: White fish brings lean protein in a gentle, easy to digest porridge.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 1 cup, rinsed, soaked and frozen

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Rinse the rice, soak it 30 minutes, drain, and freeze it at least 2 hours; the frozen grains break down fast.
Marinate the fish with a little salt, white pepper, the oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, egg white and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Bring the water and stock to a boil, add the frozen rice, and boil hard 10 minutes, stirring, then simmer 10 to 15 minutes until thick and creamy.
Season with salt, add the ginger, and slide in the fish. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes until just opaque.
Stir in the lettuce and serve topped with scallion, cilantro, sesame oil and white pepper.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the white fish and egg white.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Fish Congee
Wikipedia, Congee

recipes.name: Zongzi (Sticky Rice Dumplings)
recipes.flavorProfile: Glutinous rice wrapped in bamboo leaves around fatty pork, salted egg yolk, sausage and peanuts, slow-boiled until tender and fragrant with the leaves.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork, egg yolk and peanuts bring protein and fats, though zongzi are dense and rich, so one is a full snack.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

instructions: Marinate the pork belly with the sugar, Shaoxing wine, white pepper and a pinch of salt overnight in the refrigerator.
Drain the rice and peanuts and mix them with the soy sauce, salt and oil.

Overlap 2 leaves, fold them into a cone, and spoon in some rice. Add a piece of pork, half a yolk and a piece of sausage, cover with more rice, fold the leaves over, and tie the parcel tightly with string. Repeat to make 15.
Put the zongzi in a large pot, cover with water by 5 cm, and bring to a boil. Simmer, covered, 6 to 8 hours, topping up with boiling water so they stay covered.
Lift them out, drain, and unwrap to eat warm.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork, egg yolk and peanuts.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Zongzi, Cantonese Style
Wikipedia, Zongzi
