recipes.name: Lap Cheong Fan (Chinese Sausage Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy jasmine rice soaked with the sweet, savoury fat of Chinese sausage steamed on top, with a drizzle of soy and fresh scallion.
recipes.healthBenefit: A simple one-pot rice, with the sausage bringing flavour and some protein, though it is sweet, salty and fatty.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Put the rinsed rice and water in a rice cooker or heavy pot and lay the sausage on top.
Cook as usual, about 20 minutes, or bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat 15 to 18 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes without lifting the lid. Mix the soy sauces, sugar and sesame oil with 1 tablespoon of hot water.
Fluff the rice with the sausage, drizzle with the sauce and top with scallion.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sausage and soy sauce.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Chinese Sausage Rice (Rice Cooker)

recipes.name: Char Siu Fan (Barbecued Pork on Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, glossy, smoky slices of barbecued pork over steamed rice with tender greens and a spoon of savoury sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Char siu brings protein and the greens add vitamins, though the glaze is sweet.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Blanch the choy sum in boiling water with the oil 1 to 2 minutes and drain.
Simmer the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, water and any char siu juices 1 minute for the sauce.
Warm the char siu slices 2 to 3 minutes in a low oven, about 300°F (150°C), or in a pan.
Spoon the rice onto plates, lay the char siu and greens over it, and pour the sauce over. Scatter with scallion.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Chinese BBQ Pork (Cha Siu)
Wikipedia, Char siu

recipes.name: Suan La Tang (Hot and Sour Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, peppery, tangy broth full of pork, tofu, mushrooms, lily buds and bamboo, with ribbons of egg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork, tofu and egg bring protein and the mushrooms and bamboo add fibre, in a broth light in fat.

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear fungus, dried
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the pork with 1 teaspoon of cornstarch and a little water. Stir-fry it in the oil with the chili 1 to 2 minutes until it changes colour.
Add the stock, lily buds, wood ear and shiitake, bring to a boil, and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the two tofus and the bamboo and simmer 3 minutes. Season with the salt, sugar, white pepper, soy sauces and vinegar.
Stir the rest of the cornstarch into the water and pour it in slowly, stirring, until the soup coats a spoon.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork, tofu and egg.
From the wood ear, shiitake, lily buds and bamboo.

recipes.name: Dan Hua Tang (Egg Drop Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A silky, golden chicken broth with soft wisps of egg, a breath of sesame and white pepper, and scallion.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, warming broth with protein from the eggs.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Bring the stock to a simmer and season it with the sesame oil, salt, sugar, white pepper and turmeric.
Mix the cornstarch with the water, pour it in slowly while stirring, and simmer 1 minute until the soup thickens.
Stir the soup in one direction and pour the eggs in a thin stream so they set in ribbons, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, add the scallion and serve.

recipes.name: Wonton Soup
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender pork and greens wontons floating in a clear, savoury chicken broth with bok choy and scallion.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and the bok choy adds greens, in a broth light in fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: part finely chopped for the filling, the rest left whole

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Blanch the bok choy 30 seconds, rinse cold, squeeze dry, and finely chop half of it.
Mix the pork with the chopped greens, 1 1/2 tablespoons of sesame oil, half the white pepper, the soy sauce, half the salt, the Shaoxing wine and water, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper, wet the edges, fold into a triangle, and bring the two corners together. Make about 40.
Season the stock with the rest of the salt, sesame oil and white pepper and keep it hot.
Boil the wontons in a separate pot 3 to 5 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked, adding the rest of the bok choy for the last minute.
Lift the wontons and greens into bowls, ladle the stock over, and top with scallion.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Wonton Soup
Wikipedia, Wonton

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life wonton soup: pork and bok choy filling seasoned with sesame oil, soy, Shaoxing wine and white pepper, boiled separately and served in seasoned stock. Wonton Wrappers base, 40 of 60, and Qing Tang 6 cups. 6 bowls.

recipes.name: Dong Gua Tang (Winter Melon Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, mild, gently sweet pork rib broth with soft, translucent winter melon and ginger.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light broth with protein from the pork ribs and water-rich winter melon, low in fat once skimmed.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Cover the ribs with cold water, bring to a boil, boil 2 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Put the ribs, ginger and water in a pot, bring to a boil, and simmer gently, partly covered, 75 to 90 minutes.
Add the winter melon and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until it is translucent and tender.
Season with salt and white pepper and serve with cilantro and scallion.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Winter Melon Soup with Pork Ribs
Wikipedia, Winter melon soup

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life winter melon and pork rib soup: blanched ribs simmered with ginger about 90 minutes, then winter melon 15 minutes, salt and white pepper. 8 bowls.

recipes.name: Su Mi Geng (Sweet Corn Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, gently sweet corn soup with soft chicken and silky white egg, seasoned with white pepper and sesame.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken and egg white bring lean protein and the corn adds fibre.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 tsp for the chicken, the rest in the slurry

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the chicken with the water, 1 teaspoon of cornstarch and the oyster sauce and leave 15 minutes.
Bring the stock to a boil with the corn and turmeric and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the chicken, breaking it up, and simmer 2 minutes until it is cooked.
Mix the rest of the cornstarch with 120 ml of the stock or water and stir it in until the soup thickens, 1 minute.
Season with salt, white pepper and sesame oil, then pour in the egg whites in a thin stream while stirring. Top with scallion and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken and egg whites.

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life chicken and corn egg drop soup, the Cantonese su mi geng: creamed corn simmered in stock with velveted minced chicken, thickened with cornstarch, egg whites drizzled in. Qing Tang 5 cups. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Xi Hu Niu Rou Geng (West Lake Beef Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A silky, thickened broth with fine minced beef, soft tofu, mushrooms and wisps of egg white, finished with cilantro and white pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef, tofu and egg whites bring protein in a light, gentle soup.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 tsp for the beef, the rest in the slurry

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the beef with a pinch of salt, the Shaoxing wine and 2 teaspoons of cornstarch. Blanch it in boiling water 30 seconds, stirring to separate, and drain.
Bring the stock to a boil with the ginger, add the tofu and mushrooms, and simmer 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the beef and return to a boil, skimming any foam.
Stir the rest of the cornstarch into the water and pour it in slowly, stirring, until the soup thickens.
Season with salt and white pepper, drizzle in the egg whites in a thin stream, and stir in the cilantro and scallion.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, tofu and egg whites.

citations.source: Omnivore's Cookbook, West Lake Beef Soup

recipes.curationNote: Omnivore's Cookbook West Lake beef soup: minced beef seasoned and blanched, simmered in stock with soft tofu and mushrooms, thickened with cornstarch, egg whites and cilantro to finish. Named for West Lake in Hangzhou and common in Cantonese restaurants. Only one source could be opened. Qing Tang 6 cups. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Lian Ou Pai Gu Tang (Lotus Root and Pork Rib Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, sweet, savoury broth from long-simmered pork ribs, with soft, starchy lotus root, kelp and goji berries.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork ribs bring protein and the lotus root adds fibre and vitamin C, in a broth light in fat once skimmed.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Cover the ribs with cold water, bring to a boil, boil 2 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Put the ribs, lotus root, kelp, ginger and water in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming.
Simmer gently, partly covered, 3 to 4 hours, until the lotus root is soft and the broth is rich.
Add the goji berries for the last 10 minutes, season with salt, and serve with scallion.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Lotus Root Pork Soup

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life lotus root and pork rib soup: blanched ribs simmered for hours with lotus root, optional kelp, ginger and goji berries. The source gives about 4 hours; 3 to 4 hours is given. A Wuhan and Cantonese home soup. Only one source could be opened. 12 bowls.

recipes.name: Fan Qie Dan Hua Tang (Tomato Egg Drop Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A bright, tangy tomato broth with soft egg ribbons, a little sesame and fresh herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene and the egg adds protein, in a light soup.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Heat the oil over medium heat and cook the tomatoes 3 to 5 minutes, pressing them, until they soften and release their juice.
Add the stock and water, bring to a boil, and simmer 3 to 5 minutes.
Season with the soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper and salt, and stir in the cornstarch mixed with water.
Stir the soup and pour in the egg in a thin stream, then turn off the heat and add the scallion and cilantro.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Tomato Egg Drop Soup
Wikipedia, Tomato and egg soup

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life tomato egg drop soup: tomatoes cooked down in oil, simmered with stock and water, seasoned with soy, sesame oil and white pepper, lightly thickened and finished with egg. Qing Tang 1 cup. 4 bowls.

recipes.name: Yu Tou Dou Fu Tang (Fish Head and Tofu Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A milky white, rich fish broth from a seared fish head boiled hard, with silky tofu, ginger, red dates and goji.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish and tofu bring protein, and the fish head adds calcium and omega-3 fats to the broth.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Rub the fish head with a little salt and leave 10 minutes, then pat it dry.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium high heat, add the ginger, and sear the fish head 3 to 4 minutes a side until golden.
Pour in the Shaoxing wine, then the boiling water, and boil hard over high heat 10 to 15 minutes, until the broth turns milky white.
Add the jujubes and tofu and simmer 10 minutes, then the goji for 2 minutes.
Season with salt, sugar and white pepper, add a few drops of sesame oil, and serve with scallion and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tofu and fish bones.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Milky Fish Soup with Tofu

recipes.curationNote: Woks of Life milky fish and tofu soup: fish seared in oil with ginger, boiling water added and boiled hard until the broth turns white, then tofu, red dates and goji. The source uses a whole carp; this dish calls for the fish head, so a fish head is used in its place, cooked the same way. Scaled to 4 servings. Only one source could be opened.

recipes.name: Ma La Huo Guo (Sichuan Hot Pot)
recipes.flavorProfile: A bubbling, fiery, numbing broth of chili, Sichuan pepper and fermented bean paste in which thin meats, tofu, mushrooms and greens are cooked at the table.
recipes.healthBenefit: The dippers bring protein from beef and tofu and plenty of vegetables, though the broth is oily and salty, so most of it is left in the pot.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Tofu, firm, prepared with calcium sulfate and magnesium chloride (nigari)
Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear fungus, dried
Glass noodles made from mung bean starch

instructions: Soak the dried chilies in hot water 10 minutes, drain, and chop them roughly.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium low heat. Add the garlic, ginger and scallion and fry 3 to 5 minutes until golden.

Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans and fry 3 to 5 minutes until the oil turns deep red. Add the chilies, Sichuan pepper and the whole spices and fry 2 to 3 minutes more, stirring so nothing burns.
Add the rock sugar, Shaoxing wine and stock and bring to a boil, then simmer 15 to 20 minutes.

Set the pot on a burner at the table at a steady simmer. Cook the dippers in it a few at a time: thin beef 10 to 30 seconds, greens and enoki 1 to 2 minutes, tofu, lotus root, potato and noodles 3 to 5 minutes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the vegetables, mushrooms and lotus root.
From the doubanjiang and black beans in the broth.
